question_type: visual chart count (local maxima on line plots of a printed page); plotted data absent from the text corpus
decisive_step: There is no decisive selection step: printed page 5 of treasury_bulletin_1990_09.txt (page marker at line 406, next marker at line 461) holds Exhibit 1 (lines 410-419, a cross-country 1960-1988 comparison, most likely bars/scatter) and Exhibit 2 (lines 421-459, a 1898-1990 saving-ratio line chart), but the corpus keeps only chart titles, axis ticks and annotations, never the plotted line. The reference (worklog step 3 'Key finding', worklog step 4 dead-end grep/FTS, solution.json decision 3) reached the same page and then estimated the count from an approximate series recalled from memory (calc.py), and was graded wrong. All four cells and the reference produced five different counts.

a.path_summary: Read README, found the 1990_09 file with the officeqa helper (a[6]-a[10]), mapped printed page 5 to lines ~390-475 (a[24]) and identified Exhibits 1 and 2. From a[26] it fell into an exact 6-step cycle (rg for the two exhibit titles -> rg for the article title across issues -> sqlite3 .schema on corpus.sqlite) repeated ~137 times through a[846]: 447 requests, 3272 s, 56 M input tokens. At a[847] its notes say 'We have summary', i.e. the client's own context compaction apparently reset it; it then re-read README and the page (a[849]-a[853]), confirmed no plotted coordinates (a[855]), searched for the article elsewhere and for image/PDF traces (a[866]-a[894]) and answered a guessed integer at a[896] without calc or submit.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Started re-running the same three read-only commands (rg exhibit titles, rg article title, sqlite3 .schema) whose outputs never changed, ~137 cycles, until an external context reset at a[847]; the eventual answer at a[896] is a guess because the plotted values do not exist in the corpus (EXTERNAL_KNOWLEDGE would be the stage of the guess itself).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell was right. The reference (worklog step 4) did one grep and two FTS searches, concluded 'no reprint or data table exists', and moved on to an explicit low-confidence estimate within 11 steps.

tool_use.friction: Runaway identical-command loop a[26]-a[846] (~137 repeats of a 3-command cycle, 3272 s, 56 M input tokens) with no harness note in this text-only cell; BSD find lacks -printf (a[20]-a[21]); ls of the parent dir denied by the OS (a[862]); pkg_resources missing (a[884]).

a.text_use: none acted on; the 'Loops: a command repeated with the same output will not change' sentence was in AGENTS.md and was ignored for ~820 steps

b.path_summary: Same opening as a (README, officeqa helper, sed of the file head), then rg for exhibit strings (b[15]) and nl/sed of lines 400-510 (b[17]) to pin printed page 5 and its two exhibits. Checked that the corpus holds only .txt files (b[19]-b[21]), read the chart OCR (b[24]-b[26]), searched for the underlying series or a reprint in other issues (b[29]-b[37]). Then repeated a 4-step cycle three times (b[37]/b[41]/b[45] rg 'Scadding', b[39]/b[43] find on the agent dir); the loop guard fired at call 21 and it submitted a guessed count (b[48]).

first_divergence.what_it_did: With the page identified and no plotted values anywhere in the corpus, it guessed a small count ('visible peak count') from its own notion of the chart rather than from any evidence.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: No cell was right; the reference guessed a much larger count from a memory-reconstructed annual series and was also wrong.

tool_use.friction: A 4-step identical loop (b[37]-b[45], 3 repeats) stopped by the loop guard at call 21; BSD find -printf error (b[19]-b[20]).

b.harness_use: Loop note at call 21 (exact command issued 3 times, identical output; options: submit or run something new) ended the loop, b submitted immediately after (b[48]). Gate: submit accepted with no findings (api/checks/001.json: fired=[]). The harness changed cost (156 s vs a's 3272 s) but not the answer.

smallest_change.change: Keep the mech-static loop guard and enable it in the text cells too: when the same shell command has been issued N=3 times with byte-identical output, insert the note the b cell saw ('You have issued this exact command 3 times: <cmd>. Its output was identical each time. Current candidates: <list or none>. Options: submit --answer "<A>" for a candidate you trust, or run a command you have not run yet.'). On this question that note ended b's loop at call 21 (156 s); cell a, which had only the AGENTS.md sentence about loops, repeated an identical 3-command cycle ~137 times from a[26] to a[846] (3272 s, 447 requests, 56 M input tokens) and was rescued only by the client's own context compaction at a[847]. Also add a hard cap (e.g. after the third note, or after 30 identical repeats, the harness stops the episode and takes the best candidate or an empty answer) so a text-only cell cannot burn an hour on one question.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: the note only fires on byte-identical command+output triples and only offers options; on ordinal 11 no cell tripped it

alternatives.change: Add to AGENTS.md: 'The corpus is text only. Charts survive as their title, axis ticks and annotations; the plotted line, page images and PDFs do not exist here or anywhere else on disk (there is nothing behind corpus.sqlite either). If a question asks for something only visible in a chart, do not search for images or hidden files: say what the page holds and give your best estimate at once.' Every cell spent 15-50 steps looking for images, PDFs, sqlite blobs, hidden workspace files or a reprint (a[20]-a[30], b[19]-b[27], b2[15]-b2[32], c[11]-c[43]).
alternatives.why_not_first: It would cut cost, not fix the answer; and a text sentence about loops was already ignored by a, so a sentence about charts might be too. Useful as a cost control, officeqa_specific.

alternatives.change: Give the submit gate an 'unverifiable' path: if no calc run and no show_table/printings cell backs the submitted number and the question mentions a page/chart/plot, the gate says so ('No table cell or calc output matches this answer; this looks like a visual question the corpus cannot answer. Submit your best estimate with --keep "estimate"') instead of silently accepting. b2 explicitly submitted hoping for feedback (b2[40]) and got none.
alternatives.why_not_first: Does not change correctness; only makes the guess explicit in the ledger and stops the 'submit as oracle' behaviour.

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the loop sentence ('Loops: a command repeated with the same output will not change...') in AGENTS.md and still repeated the same three commands ~137 times; the only cell whose loop stopped early was b, which had no advice text but had the runtime loop note. Text does not act once the model is inside a repetition; a runtime insert does.
fix.irreducible: Yes for correctness: the count of local maxima requires the plotted line of Exhibit 2 (and possibly Exhibit 1), which is not in the text corpus (worklog step 3 'Key finding', step 4 dead end; the corpus holds only titles, axis ticks and the annotations at lines 444-451). The reference's memory-based estimate was also wrong. No text, tool or control change can make a text-only agent count peaks on an absent chart. The question is also loosely worded ('Monthly Bulletin' for a quarterly issue; plural 'line plots' for one line chart plus a likely scatter).

notes: Design points for v10. (1) The loop guard is the single clearest control win in this question: identical evidence in a and b, 20x cost difference, and the text-only cell escaped only through an external compaction (a[847] 'We have summary'); a text cell with no compaction would have run until the request/time budget. Consider a hard stop after the third loop note. (2) The four table tools are irrelevant to chart questions, and none of the cells tried them, so the tool layer is not at fault; a small 'page' helper (print the lines between two page markers of an issue, e.g. lines 406-460, with a one-line note 'charts: titles/axes/annotations only, no plotted values') would have replaced the nl/sed hunting in every cell and pre-empted the image search. (3) The gate gave no signal on an unverifiable answer; b2 submitted precisely to probe it (b2[40]-b2[41]). (4) Exhibit 2's OCR prints the y-axis ticks twice (lines ~421-459), which c[46] misread as 'two line plots side by side'; a page helper could suppress or label repeated axis blocks. (5) The v8 divergence analysis file listed in index.json (per-question/047.json) does not exist; v8 covered only GLM-fail/Opus-pass questions, and this one was wrong in every arm including Opus.
